title: Festival Dolls Dyed in the Setting Sun
notes: Non-murder case (theft, no human victim); label.murderer_id is reused per dataset convention to mean 'culprit_id' (the thief). Detective Boys and other recurring cast (Conan, Ayumi, Genta, Mitsuhiko, Haibara, the unnamed inspector/officer) omitted by convention -- they narrate/assist but are not suspects, victims, or witnesses under investigation. Also omitted as orthogonal to this case: the unrelated Haibara/Miyano-family backstory dialogue that appears mid-episode (about her father Miyano Atsushi) -- it does not bear on the doll-festival theft. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. Old low-fidelity file (cases/ep312-313...) correctly named all four suspects and correctly identified Yayoi Kanno (its s2) as the culprit -- this rebuild CONFIRMS that call, unlike several other rebuilds where the old culprit was wrong. One factual correction versus the old file: it described the scroll as hidden 'under the clothing of a display doll'; the transcript instead shows it was hidden under the red felt cloth *on top of* the 7-tier doll stand, reached by climbing the tiers like a staircase -- the old file's clue text conflated the doll-displacement clue with the hiding method. The old file also collapsed the mystery into a single clue (Kyoto doll-arrangement convention); the actual fair-play chain has five distinct comparative facts (photo comparison, physical-inconsistency reasoning, the Kyoto-vs-Tokyo convention, staged-burglary behavioral tells, and the fax-timestamp window), all modeled here as separate clue nodes. Per CONSTRUCTION.md's temporal-fields note, order/temporal_frame/years_before_present are omitted throughout. case_type: theft.

clues.desc: Camera photos show the Emperor/Empress dolls swapped and 13 others shifted between the two shopping-trip photos

Only the top two dolls were swapped, not knocked to the floor -- too controlled for an accidental collision, consistent with someone deliberately climbing the tiers rather than crashing into the stand
The swap matches the old Kyoto convention (male doll on the left) that modern Tokyo stores reverse -- only someone raised in the old tradition would default to it
A 'burglar' ignored a fax machine mid-delivery, left a purse in plain sight, ransacked only two rooms, and took only the one item whose price they already knew
Fax pages all timestamped 3:28 PM were still arriving when the group left and had finished by the time they returned near 3:40 PM, narrowing the theft to the ten minutes Yayoi Kanno was home alone
